sentences.zh: 而且他们没有自己的巴勒斯坦国这一事实，将永远是中东任何积极发展的巨大障碍。

sentences.en: Those people are open to negotiate an Israeli withdrawal and an establishment of a Palestinian state, and they are primarily interested in Israel's security over everything else.
sentences.zh: 这些人对通过谈判实现以色列撤军以及建立巴勒斯坦国持开放态度，他们最关心的首要问题是以色列的安全。

sentences.en: Security, to them, means not just defending yourself from outside forces, but also having a democratic, lawful state.
sentences.zh: 对他们而言，安全不仅意味着抵御外部势力的防卫，还意味着拥有一个民主、法治的国家。

sentences.en: And what about the other side?
sentences.zh: 那另一方呢？

sentences.en: The people who want to make territory like the West Bank part of Israel permanently.
sentences.zh: 那些希望将约旦河西岸等领土永久并入以色列的人。

sentences.en: Who are they and what's their backstory?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？他们的背景故事是什么？

sentences.en: You know, it's not monolithic, but broadly speaking, there are like two groups.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并不是铁板一块，但广义上讲，大约有两个群体。

sentences.en: One, let's call them secular right-wingers.
sentences.zh: 第一类，我们称他们为世俗右翼分子。

sentences.en: They potentially could discuss an establishment of a Palestinian state, but they say that from a sheer point of security,
sentences.zh: 他们理论上可能会讨论建立一个巴勒斯坦国，但他们表示，从纯粹的安全角度来看，

sentences.en: it would be much safer for Israel to control the West Bank rather than to give the West Bank to another state, another entity that they are concerned will become hostile to Israel.
sentences.zh: 由以色列控制约旦河西岸，要比把约旦河西岸交给另一个他们担心会变得对以色列充满敌意的国家或实体要安全得多。

sentences.en: And then there is another group who are looking at the situation from a very different point of view.
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一个群体，他们从一个截然不同的角度看待这个局势。

sentences.en: They believe that by actually controlling these lands,
sentences.zh: 他们相信，通过实际控制这些土地，

sentences.en: they could hasten the arrival of the Messiah.
sentences.zh: 他们可以加速弥赛亚的到来。

sentences.en: And in order to make sure that this Messiah will come as soon as possible, the right way to do that would be to establish settlements in those occupied territories
sentences.zh: 为了确保这位弥赛亚尽早到来，正确的做法就是在这些被占领土上建立定居点，

sentences.en: to make sure they will never be given back to an Arab nation or Palestinian people.
sentences.zh: 以确保它们永远不会被归还给阿拉伯国家或巴勒斯坦人民。

sentences.en: But Israel got control over these territories in the war.
sentences.zh: 但是以色列是在战争中获得这些领土的控制权的。

sentences.en: So why does this need to settle them?
sentences.zh: 那为什么还需要在上面建立定居点呢？

sentences.en: So the official relationship is it's an occupied territory.
sentences.zh: 所以官方的定性是，这是被占领土。

sentences.en: And occupied territory, according to international law,
sentences.zh: 而根据国际法，被占领土上，

sentences.en: everybody are under the authority of the military commander and under the rule of military law.
sentences.zh: 所有人都受军事指挥官的管辖，并受军事法的管辖。

sentences.en: But many of those ultra-nationalist religious Israelis, they realize that military can be ordered to evacuate during some kind of a peace treaty
sentences.zh: 但许多超民族主义的宗教以色列人意识到，在某种和平条约期间，军方可能会被命令撤离，

sentences.en: because military does what it's told to do.
sentences.zh: 因为军方执行的是下达给它的命令。

sentences.en: But when you have, at the beginning, small outposts, then settlements, then cities,
sentences.zh: 但当你拥有了——起初是小型前哨站，然后是定居点，再到城市——

sentences.en: those are going to be very hard to evacuate.
sentences.zh: 这些地方将变得非常难以撤离。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Israel gets this land.
sentences.zh: 所以以色列得到了这片土地。

sentences.en: And some Israelis see this land as leverage, something to trade with Arab adversaries or for a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 一些以色列人将这片土地视为筹码，可以用来与阿拉伯对手交易，或者换取一个巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: But this other group of religious ultra-nationalists are like, no, all that land is ours by divine right.
sentences.zh: 但另一群宗教极右翼民族主义者却认为，不，所有这些土地根据神圣权利都属于我们。

sentences.en: And we don't ever want to trade this land away for anything.
sentences.zh: 而且我们绝不想为了任何东西把这片土地出让。

sentences.en: And the best way to prevent the land from being given away is by settling the land themselves,
sentences.zh: 防止这片土地被送出去的最好方法，就是由他们自己去这片土地上建立定居点，

sentences.en: knowing that it would be harder to give away if there are Jewish Israelis living there.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道，如果有以色列犹太人住在那里，土地就更难割让了。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: But there's one small problem.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个小问题。

sentences.en: It was illegal under the military orders, the military that governs these territories.
sentences.zh: 根据军令，即管辖这些领土的军队的命令，这是非法的。

sentences.en: So what these religious ultra-nationalists wanted to do is just not allowed by the state.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些宗教极右翼民族主义者想要做的事，根本不被国家允许。

sentences.en: But they started taking action towards that goal anyway.
sentences.zh: 但他们无论如何还是朝着这个目标采取了行动。

sentences.en: So the central ultra-nationalist religious group was called Gush Emunim, the block of the faithful.
sentences.zh: 当时，核心的宗教极右翼民族主义组织被称为“古什·埃穆尼姆”（Gush Emunim），即信徒集团。

sentences.en: And so one day in 1975, they, Gush Emunim, suddenly came to a deserted Jordanian military camp in the West Bank and declared that this is their outpost,
sentences.zh: 于是在1975年的某一天，他们——古什·埃穆尼姆——突然来到约旦河西岸的一个荒废约旦军事营地，宣布这里是他们的前哨站，

sentences.en: bloody violating orders from the military that this is totally, totally illegal.
sentences.zh: 公然违反军方关于这完全、彻底非法的命令。

sentences.en: And instead of ordering the military,
sentences.zh: 然而，时任军方负责人并没有下令让军队……

sentences.en: Shimon Peres, who was in charge of the military, the IDF, and therefore in charge of the West Bank, he was not a settler or an ultra-nationalist supporter in any way.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·佩雷斯（Shimon Peres）当时掌管军队、以色列国防军（IDF），因此也掌管约旦河西岸，他绝不是定居者或极右翼民族主义的支持者。

sentences.en: I don't think he liked them.
sentences.zh: 我想他并不喜欢他们。

sentences.en: But fearing to confront them and their base, he allowed them to stay.
sentences.zh: 但由于害怕与他们及其支持基础发生对抗，他允许他们留了下来。

sentences.en: And in order not to call that just impunity and disregarding the law that he was supposed to enforce, he called that a working camp.
sentences.zh: 为了不把这直接称为有罪不罚、无视他本应执行的法律，他称之为一个工作营。

sentences.en: And so Peres was creating an alibi for himself and for the state.
sentences.zh: 因此，佩雷斯是在为自己和国家制造不在场证明。

sentences.en: And those tricks, this euphemism, this laundering of words and terminology
sentences.zh: 这些伎俩、这种委婉说法、这种对词汇和术语的粉饰，

sentences.en: is a first move that showed the settlers that even if they do something that is bluntly illegal, if they are stubborn enough, they will win.
sentences.zh: 是向定居者展示的第一步，即他们即使做了明显非法的事，只要足够顽固，就能取得胜利。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which seems like it would only embolden them to learn that they can get away with breaking the law.
sentences.zh: 这似乎只会助长他们的气焰，让他们知道自己违法也能逃脱惩罚。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It gave them massive backwind.
sentences.zh: 这给了他们巨大的东风。

sentences.en: And so that early settlement, it grew.
sentences.zh: 于是，那个早期的定居点发展壮大起来。

sentences.en: It grew into many more settlements that spread across the West Bank and eventually some years later to Gaza.
sentences.zh: 它发展成了更多的定居点，遍布整个约旦河西岸，并在几年后最终延伸到了加沙。

sentences.en: And that point in the late 70s, the settlement project by those ultra-nationalists was fully underway.
sentences.zh: 到了70年代末，那些极右翼民族主义者的定居点项目已经全面展开。

sentences.en: And they thought they wouldn't have any more resistance because in 1977, for the first time in Israel history, the right, the Likud party, is in control of the country.
sentences.zh: 他们原以为不会再遇到什么阻力，因为在1977年，以色列历史上第一次，右翼的利库德集团掌控了国家。

sentences.en: And it's led by Menachem Begim.
sentences.zh: 并且由梅纳赫姆·贝京（Menachem Begin）领导。

sentences.en: And typically, leaders on the right were supportive of the settlement, not so eager to negotiate with Arab neighbors peace in return for land.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，右翼领导人支持定居点建设，并不那么渴望与阿拉伯邻国通过土地换和平进行谈判。

sentences.en: But Begim surprised everybody.
sentences.zh: 但贝京让所有人都大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Peace now celebrates a great victory for the nations of Egypt and Israel and for all mankind.
sentences.zh: “现在和平”庆祝埃及和以色列两国以及全人类的伟大胜利。

sentences.en: At the first part of his term, he signs a historical peace accord with Egypt.
sentences.zh: 在他任期的初期，他与埃及签署了一项历史性的和平协议。

sentences.en: The committee summited Camp David is over and Israel and Egypt have agreed to two documents taking a giant step toward achieving peace in their troubled corner of the world.
sentences.zh: 戴维营峰会委员会已经结束，以色列和埃及已就两份文件达成一致，向在这个充满麻烦的世界角落实现和平迈出了巨大的一步。

sentences.en: And in return for peace, he gives back the whole of the Sinai Peninsula
sentences.zh: 作为对和平的回报，他归还了整个西奈半岛，

sentences.en: after evacuating the Jewish-Israeli settlements from there.
sentences.zh: 在从那里撤出以色列犹太人定居点之后。

sentences.en: On Israel's side, it seems that Begim has agreed to negotiate the removal of Israeli settlements from the Sinai.
sentences.zh: 在以色列方面，看来贝京已经同意通过谈判撤除西奈半岛的以色列定居点。

sentences.en: So Israel negotiates a way of land for peace.
sentences.zh: 因此，以色列通过谈判走了一条土地换和平的道路。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, both Sadat and Begim are left with the responsibility of selling those concessions to their own constituencies.
sentences.zh: 现在，萨达特和贝京都面临着向各自选民兜售这些让步的责任。

sentences.en: So while the Menachem Begim government
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然梅纳赫姆·贝京政府

sentences.en: supported the ongoing settlement campaign, it also gave back territory that the settlers thought should not be given back at any price, at any cost, at any term,
sentences.zh: 支持持续进行的定居点运动，但它也归还了定居者认为无论付出什么代价、任何情况、任何条款都不应归还的领土，

sentences.en: because they are part of the biblical land of Israel.
sentences.zh: 因为它们是圣经中以色列土地的一部分。

sentences.en: And they saw that as a threat, that it will happen again.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一种威胁，担心这种事会再次发生。

sentences.en: That more land might be bartered away.
sentences.zh: 更多土地可能会被当作筹码交易出去。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula led to an outburst of violence from the settlers.
sentences.zh: 因此，从西奈半岛撤军引发了定居者的暴力爆发。

sentences.en: Some extreme settlers wanted to signal to the Israeli government that they would cause chaos if any more land is negotiated away with the Arab countries.
sentences.zh: 一些极端定居者希望向以色列政府发出信号，如果再拿任何土地与阿拉伯国家进行领土谈判，他们就会制造混乱。

sentences.en: And so they start attacking Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始袭击约旦河西岸和加沙的巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: And then in June of 1980, what was later called the Jewish Underground, which was an extremist offshoot within the settler movement, attempted to blow up
sentences.zh: 接着在1980年6月，后来被称为“犹太地下组织”（Jewish Underground）的极端分子——定居者运动内部的一个极端分支，试图炸毁

sentences.en: three prominent Palestinian mayors in the West Bank.
sentences.zh: 约旦河西岸的三位杰出巴勒斯坦市长。

sentences.en: They put bombs in the cars and severely injured two of them.
sentences.zh: 他们在汽车里放置了炸弹，并重伤了其中两人。

sentences.en: And so once these attacks happened, some senior officials said, the military just failed to condemn them.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些袭击发生后，一些高级官员表示，军方根本没有谴责这些行为。

sentences.en: What did they say?
sentences.zh: 他们说了什么？

sentences.en: They said, this is welcome.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这大快人心。

sentences.en: The military commander of the West Bank, when referred to the bombs that hit the lower part of the body of the mayors, he said, it's a pity they did not aim higher.
sentences.zh: 约旦河西岸的军事指挥官在谈到炸伤市长身体下半部的炸弹时说：“很遗憾他们没有瞄准更高一点。”

sentences.en: Hinting that he wished they died.
sentences.zh: 暗示他希望他们死掉。

sentences.en: Now, when the settlers, when the members of this group, the Jewish Underground, when they hear the military commander of the area saying something like that, they understand what,
sentences.zh: 现在，当定居者、这个组织的成员“犹太地下组织”听到该地区的军事指挥官说出这样的话时，他们明白，

sentences.en: you know, everybody would understand.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有人都会明白的。

sentences.en: This is an encouragement.
sentences.zh: 这是一种鼓励。

sentences.en: This is not contaminant.
sentences.zh: 这不是谴责。

sentences.en: This is not enforcing the law.
sentences.zh: 这不是在执法。

sentences.en: This is a sort of a wicked nod with a smile, with humor.
sentences.zh: 这是一种带着微笑、带着幽默的邪恶默许。

sentences.en: Why didn't they have higher?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们没瞄准更高？

sentences.en: They should have killed them.
sentences.zh: 他们本该杀了他们。

sentences.en: So this is a very clear sign from the people who were supposed to be enforcing the law that violence toward Palestinians is not only not bad, it might even be good.
sentences.zh: 所以，这来自本应执法的人员，是一个非常明确的信号，表明针对巴勒斯坦人的暴力不仅不是坏事，甚至可能是件好事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Ronan, in this period of the 1980s, were Israelis trying to fight back against this apathy toward Palestinian lives and just general disregard for the rule of law
sentences.zh: 那么罗南，在20世纪80年代这段时期，以色列人是否曾试图反击这种对巴勒斯坦人生命的冷漠以及对法治的普遍蔑视，

sentences.en: in the West Bank?
sentences.zh: 就在约旦河西岸？

sentences.en: I assume Israelis would be appalled.
sentences.zh: 我猜以色列人会感到震惊。

sentences.en: I don't think theoretically that you are wrong, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，从理论上讲，我认为你没有错。

sentences.en: I just think that they didn't know the people in Israel, the public, they didn't know what is happening there.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得他们并不知道，以色列的人民、公众，他们根本不知道那里正在发生什么。

sentences.en: It's remote, relative remote to distances in Israel.
sentences.zh: 那里很偏远，相对以色列的国土距离来说。

sentences.en: The press was almost not covering anything that happened there, but there were people who got, made aware of the situation, this impunity, and they realized how horrible
sentences.zh: 媒体几乎没有报道任何在那里发生的事情，但确实有一些人注意到了这种情况、这种有罪不罚现象，他们意识到

sentences.en: the situation is.
sentences.zh: 情况有多么可怕。

sentences.en: So a group of law professors from both the Tel Aviv and the Jerusalem
sentences.zh: 因此，来自特拉维夫和耶路撒冷希伯来

sentences.en: Hebrew universities wrote a letter to the Attorney General of Israel.
sentences.zh: 大学的一群法学教授向以色列总检察长写了一封信。

sentences.en: They said, you should open an investigation about Jewish terrorism and violence.
sentences.zh: 他们说，你们应该对犹太恐怖主义和暴力事件展开调查。

sentences.en: And the Attorney General, he was appalled.
sentences.zh: 而总检察长感到震惊。

sentences.en: He didn't know as well.
sentences.zh: 他也不知道。

sentences.en: He's the Attorney General of the state, and he doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 他是国家的总检察长，但他却不知道。

sentences.en: So he calls in his deputy for special duties,
sentences.zh: 于是他召集了负责特别事务的副手朱迪斯·卡尔普（Judith Karp），

sentences.en: Judith Karp, and he assigned her to lead a committee that would go and thoroughly investigate the claims and concerns of those professors.
sentences.zh: 并指派她领导一个委员会，前去彻底调查这些教授们的说法和关切。

sentences.en: When they started to investigate, they realized that the situation on the ground is much worse than described in the professor's letter.
sentences.zh: 当他们开始调查时，他们意识到实地情况比教授信中所描述的要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: And they discovered the whole system of total negligence, inability to execute efficient and just interrogation, investigation on claims of Jewish crimes.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了一个完全疏忽的系统，无法对犹太人犯罪的指控进行高效、公正的审讯和调查。

sentences.en: they found the police that is completely incapable of doing its job and the military that in spite of being in charge of the security of the region is completely helpless
sentences.zh: 他们发现警方完全无力胜任其工作，而军队尽管负责该地区的治安，却在为巴勒斯坦居民提供这种安全保障方面

sentences.en: in supplying that security to the Palestinian inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 完全无能为力。

sentences.en: So this Karp report was pretty damning.
sentences.zh: 所以这份卡尔普报告相当具有定罪效力。

sentences.en: Pretty damning.
sentences.zh: 相当具有定罪效力。

sentences.en: And then this was so secret because, of course, the local and international implications of such a report are significant.
sentences.zh: 而且这曾是高度机密，因为当然，这样一份报告在地方和国际上的影响是巨大的。

sentences.en: But the attorney general was assured by the ministers that this will be brought to the cabinet and thoroughly discussed and there will be steps taken following that.
sentences.zh: 但总检察长向部长们保证，这将被提交给内阁并进行深入讨论，并且之后会采取措施。

sentences.en: And the long-time minister of the police invited Karp to his home to discuss the report.
sentences.zh: 这位长期的警察部长邀请卡尔普到他家讨论这份报告。

sentences.en: Now, Karp was sure that he wants to hear more, maybe to congratulate her for this work.
sentences.zh: 当时卡尔普确信他是想了解更多，也许是为她的这项工作向她表示祝贺。

sentences.en: But instead, she recalls,
sentences.zh: 但相反，她回忆说，

sentences.en: he started to attack her for what they are doing.
sentences.zh: 他开始因他们的所作所为而攻击她。

sentences.en: And soon, she realized that they are going to do nothing.
sentences.zh: 很快，她意识到他们什么都不会做。

sentences.en: They are going to bury the report,
sentences.zh: 他们打算把这份报告束之高阁，

sentences.en: which, at the end, led Karp to resign the posters leading their team because she realized nothing is going to be done.
sentences.zh: 这最终导致卡尔普辞去了团队负责人的职务，因为她意识到根本不会有任何改变。

sentences.en: And in retrospect,
sentences.zh: 回想起来，

sentences.en: Karp said, we were naive.
sentences.zh: 卡尔普说，我们当时太天真了。

sentences.en: And so, the 80s and the 90s saw a growing turmoil in the West Bank and Gaza.
sentences.zh: 因此，80年代和90年代见证了约旦河西岸和加沙日益加剧的动荡。
